column1: # The package set, and the single source of truth for it.
# BuildNugets.sh packs in this order, the release and PR workflows generate their package tables
# from it, and run-emulator-tests.sh clears the local NuGet cache for every id listed here. Adding
# a package means adding a row here and a project under src/ - nothing else has a second copy of
# the list to fall out of step with.
# Rows are in dependency order: a package's in-repo deps must already have appeared above it.
# package-id
SFMCSDK.Net.Android
# NOT BOUND, and why.
# Salesforce publishes these under com.salesforce.marketingcloud on its GitHub-Pages Maven
# repository (counted 2026-07 against the repository index). This section exists so "is X missing
# on purpose?" has an answer here rather than in someone's memory - and it doubles as the
# machine-read roster: the upstream-watch workflow reconciles the repository index against every
# artifact id named in this file and opens an issue when Salesforce grows an artifact that is
# neither bound above nor listed below. Keep every entry a FULL artifact id for that reason.
#   common-internal              Shipped INSIDE SFMCSDK.Net.Android as an unbound .aar - it is
#                                the sfmcsdk .pom's one Salesforce-internal dependency and has no
#                                public API worth a projection. Not missing; deliberately not a
#                                package of its own.
#   marketingcloudsdk            The MobilePush module family. Bound by the sibling repository,
#   pushfeaturemodule            MarketingCloudSDK.Net.Android, which depends on this package for
#   pushmodelsmodule             the core - mirroring how the native umbrella depends on sfmcsdk.
#   inappmessagingfeaturemodule
#   inappmessagingmodelsmodule
#   common
#   legacy-crypto
#   mobileappmessaging           Mobile App Messaging (MAM) - a separate, optional Salesforce
#   mobileappmessagingsdk        product on its own version line, not a dependency of either
#                                bound family. A binding candidate once a consumer asks.
#   core                         2021-era leftovers of the pre-Unified architecture, last
#   version-safety-plugin        published years before this repository existed. Dead upstream.
